summary: data (numpy, pandas, scipy), charts (matplotlib, plotly, altair, svgwrite), images (PIL, skimage), PDF (pypdf, pymupdf, pdfminer, fpdf), Word (docx, mammoth), PowerPoint (pptx), Excel (openpyxl, python_calamine), archives (zipfile, tarfile, gzip, bz2, lzma), templates (jinja2), sample data (faker), graphs (networkx), audio (soundfile), code parsing (tree_sitter: Python, Java, Go), search (rank_bm25), RDF (rdflib), WebGL (zengl) and sqlite3
brief: data, chart, image, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, audio and code-parsing packages
notes: Nothing here has a window: save charts with plt.savefig("chart.png") and use the file.

To HTML: Word with mammoth.convert_to_html, PDF with pymupdf page.get_text("xhtml"), Excel with pandas DataFrame.to_html or openpyxl, PowerPoint by reading slides with python-pptx. Open the .html in the Editor to see it.
Archives: zipfile, tarfile, gzip, bz2 and lzma in Python; zip, unzip, tar and gzip in the shell.

pymupdf.note: import pymupdf; doc = pymupdf.open("a.pdf"). Read: page.get_text() or get_text("xhtml"/"html"/"dict"). Render: page.get_pixmap(dpi=150).save("page1.png"). Edit: page.insert_text((72, 72), "text"), add_redact_annot(rect) then apply_redactions(), doc.insert_pdf(other), doc.delete_page(n), then doc.save("out.pdf").

zengl.note: zengl.init() and zengl.context() take no arguments. There is no screen (ctx.screen is 0): render into ctx.image((w, h), "rgba8unorm") and read it back. Clear with image.clear_value = (r, g, b, a), then image.clear(). Shaders are GLSL ES 3.00: start each with "#version 300 es" and "precision highp float;", and give the fragment shader "layout (location = 0) out vec4 out_color;". Per frame: ctx.new_frame(), image.clear(), pipeline.render(), ctx.end_frame(). Save: Image.frombytes("RGBA", (w, h), image.read()).save("out.png"). Formats: r/rg/rgba 8unorm, 16float, 32float, the int/uint ones and depth; no sRGB. Free what you are done with: ctx.release(image).

altair.note: No renderer and no PNG or SVG export here: chart.save("chart.json") (or chart.to_dict()) keeps the Vega-Lite spec. Draw images with matplotlib.

matplotlib.note: No window: plt.savefig("chart.png") and use the file; plt.show() shows nothing.

plotly.note: No window and no image export (kaleido is not here). fig.write_html("chart.html", include_plotlyjs="directory") writes chart.html with plotly.min.js beside it; open chart.html in the Editor and it is interactive. fig.show() shows nothing.

fpdf2.note: Built-in fonts (helvetica, times, courier) are Latin-1 only. For Vietnamese or any other script, use the DejaVu fonts matplotlib ships: fonts = matplotlib.get_data_path() + "/fonts/ttf/"; pdf.add_font("DejaVu", fname=fonts + "DejaVuSans.ttf"); pdf.add_font("DejaVu", style="B", fname=fonts + "DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf") (bold is also what table headings use); then pdf.set_font("DejaVu", size=12).

python-calamine.note: CalamineWorkbook.from_path(path).get_sheet_by_name(name).to_python() reads .xlsx, .xls and .ods; or pd.read_excel(path, engine="calamine"). To write .xlsx use openpyxl or DataFrame.to_excel.

tree-sitter.note: Grammars here: tree_sitter_python, tree_sitter_java and tree_sitter_go only (no JavaScript or TypeScript). Parser(Language(tree_sitter_python.language())).parse(source_bytes).root_node.

soundfile.note: soundfile.write("a.wav", data, rate) and soundfile.read(path) handle WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3, AIFF and more. Nothing can play sound here.

faker.note: Sample data in 110 languages: Faker("ja_JP"), Faker("zh_CN"), Faker("ko_KR"), Faker("vi_VN"), Faker("fr_FR"), Faker("de_DE"), Faker("es_ES"), Faker("pt_BR"), Faker("ru_RU"), Faker("ar_SA"), Faker("hi_IN"), Faker("th_TH")… (faker.config.AVAILABLE_LOCALES lists them all; Faker() is en_US). Faker(["en_US", "ja_JP"]) mixes them. fake.seed_instance(1) makes the data the same on every run.

pdfminer.six.note: pdfminer.high_level.extract_text(path) for the text, extract_pages(path) for its layout (text boxes with positions). It reads text a PDF has; scanned pages need OCR, which is not here.

scikit-image.note: Imports as skimage; the first import takes a few seconds (it loads scipy). skimage.io.imread/imsave read and write image files; skimage.data has sample images (camera, astronaut, coins…). No window: save results as files.
